summary.text: Scott Fetgatter is a Republican who was elected to Oklahoma House District 16 in 2016. His House biography says he served six years as chair of the House A&B Finance Committee and now leads tribal and external affairs for the House.

paragraphs.text: Fetgatter is a native of Okmulgee, Oklahoma, and moved there with his family in 1972.
Before his election he owned a construction company specializing in theme construction and also worked in sales and marketing for a web-based technology company and in the grocery business.
His House biography says that as a first-year legislator he helped extend aerospace engineering tax credits for eight years, and that he authored the Automotive Engineering Tax Credit.
In 2021 he authored the Filmed in Oklahoma Act, which created a film incentive.
Fetgatter is a Choctaw Nation citizen.
He is married to Kim, and they have two children and four grandchildren.
